title: fleet-drift-detection-and-mitigation-2026-11-07
content:
Meeting: Fleet drift detection sync / weekly operational notes
Date: 2026-11-07
Facilitator: Aisha Patel
Attendees: Leo M., Priya S., Connor W., Elena R., SRE rotation (oncall)
Channel: #infra-fleet-ops (Slack)

TL;DR:
- Automated drift-detector alerted on unexpected throughput regression in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1 between 2026-11-05 23:10 UTC and 2026-11-06 02:40 UTC.
- Root cause appears to be a combination of a new internal model kernel rollout (opt-kernel-v3) and transient host-level memory pressure from a hypervisor upgrade in a subset of hosts.
- Immediate mitigations applied: rollback kernel on affected pools, increased per-pool reserved capacity by 12%, and bumped autoscaler cooldown for the next 72h.
- Action items assigned to eng-infra and serving-runtime; follow-ups scheduled.

Scope / detection:
- Detector: fleet-drift-ml (anomaly detector comparing P50/P95 token throughput and queue depth per pool vs baseline).
- Trigger threshold: delta throughput > 18% and queue depth growth > 1.8x for 15m window.
- Alerts fired: 3 separate pools in eu-west1 (pool ids 83, 91, 93) and 2 pools in ap-southeast1 (pool ids 201, 204).
- Related metric deltas observed:
  - avg GPU utilization drop from 78% -> 61% (eu-west1, affected pools)
  - P95 generation latency increase from 310ms -> 680ms (eu-west1)
  - Queue length rose 1.9x (ap-southeast1)
  - Preemption rate briefly spiked to 6% on preemptible instances (normally <1%)

What changed before the window:
- 2026-11-05 22:50 UTC: a canary rollout of opt-kernel-v3 began in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1 (code rollout INFRA-4821). The kernel has micro-optimizations for int8 fusable paths but also a different allocator pattern.
- 2026-11-05 22:55 UTC: a maintenance patch (host kernel update) was applied to a subset of hosts in eu-west1 (patch id HK-2026-11-05-11). We observed elevated host-level RSS and swap churn after the patch in ~12% of updated hosts.

Hypothesis:
- opt-kernel-v3 interacts poorly with the updated host kernel's memory reclaim heuristics, leading to increased guest memory fragmentation and slower allocator behavior during hot inference workloads. That increases stall time per step and amplifies queueing.
- Secondary contributor: our rollout targeting logic placed canaries in the smallest pools first; those pools had little extra headroom and hit the autoscaler thresholds sooner.

Immediate mitigations taken (timeline):
- 2026-11-06 00:05 UTC: Canary rollout paused (INFRA-4821).
- 2026-11-06 00:18 UTC: opt-kernel-v3 rolled back from affected pools (PR revert: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842).
- 2026-11-06 00:25 UTC: Per-pool reserved capacity increased +12% in eu-west1 and ap-southeast1 to absorb transient queueing and reduce headroom pressure.
- 2026-11-06 01:00 UTC: Autoscaler cooldown extended from 120s -> 300s for the next 72h in affected regions to avoid oscillation while we stabilize.
- 2026-11-06 02:15 UTC: Evidence of stabilization: queue lengths trending back to baseline over subsequent hour; P95 latency returning to ~340ms by 02:40 UTC.

Observations / telemetry snippets:
- Sample event (pool 91): 2026-11-05 23:30 UTC - queue depth spike to 2.4x; downstream microservice retried 3 times causing a small ripple in host-level IO.
- Host-level monitoring showed increased /proc/slabinfo allocations coincident with the kernel update on 12 hosts.
- Memory pressure correlated with swaps on 4 hosts; those hosts were removed from rotation and reprovisioned.

Impact assessment:
- Customer-facing impact: minimal. Edge cases where tail latency briefly exceeded SLA for <45m in eu-west1 for small subset of tenants (internal tracking list maintained).
- Cost: temporary increased on-call engineering time and reserve capacity bump (~estimated incremental cost $1.9k/day if sustained).
- Risk: if unresolved, a full rollout of opt-kernel-v3 across regions would amplify the issue and could lead to longer queues and customer-visible throttling during high concurrency windows.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Eng-serving-runtime: run microbench harness for opt-kernel-v3 against host kernel versions (owner: Priya Shah) - due 2026-11-10.
- Eng-infra: reprovision and full memory-stress test for hosts patched with HK-2026-11-05-11 to validate reclaim behavior (owner: Leo Martinez) - due 2026-11-09.
- SRE/Observability: add a specific detector for slabinfo growth correlated with queue length (owner: Connor Wu) - due 2026-11-12.
- Flow routing: update rollout policy to avoid placing canaries in smallest pools and require headroom >25% (owner: Elena Rios) - propose change by 2026-11-11.
- Product & Customer Success: prepare a short internal note for customers affected by tail latency (owner: Aisha Patel) - draft by 2026-11-08.

Runbook / playbook updates recommended:
- Add a new troubleshooting step to the Fleet Runbook: when drift detector fires with memory-related signals, check host kernel patch history and slabinfo immediately.
- Add a pre-rollout checklist gating on host kernel version and available pool headroom.

Follow-ups / scheduled checkpoints:
- 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC: follow-up sync to review Priya and Leo's test results and decide on opt-kernel-v3 next steps. (Invite list: team infra, serving-runtime, SRE).
- 2026-11-12: postmortem draft (if root cause confirmed) to be posted to Confluence and linked to INFRA-4821 and INFRA-4872.

Notes / open questions:
- Could the hypervisor vendor patch have had a regression in their ballooning/reclaim heuristics? -> vendor ticket opened; contacting account rep.
- Do we need a short-term kernel freeze for hosts in critical regions during major rollouts? Pros/cons to discuss at next architecture sync.

Appendix (quick references):
- Detector runbook: Confluence:/spaces/INFRA/pages/965432/Fleet+Runbook (see section: "drift-detector triage")

Working notes (raw):
- Priya: saw allocator slowdown reproducer on the bench when running 512-conc clients at 1k tokens.
- Leo: flagged 4 repro hosts for reprovision; swapped them out 2026-11-06 01:10 UTC.
- Connor: adding metric alert to notify when slabinfo per-GPU increases >20% within 10m.
- Elena: will draft rollout-policy tweak and post to team docs for review.
